steps.caption: Black's pawn jumps two squares, past the square White's pawn attacks. White gets one chance to answer.

line.say: Black's pawn jumps two squares and lands beside White's pawn, past the square White attacks.
White captures as if the pawn had stepped one square: it lands on d6 and the pawn on d5 is removed.

claims.statement: The jump to d5 is legal.

steps.text: That is **en passant**, French for 'in passing'. When a pawn jumps two squares and lands right **beside** an enemy pawn, that pawn may capture it as if it had moved only one square, landing on the square the jumper passed over. It is optional. Ask three things about the last move: a pawn? two squares? beside my pawn? Three yeses: it is available, if it leaves your king safe.

steps.caption: The same for Black: White's pawn jumps two squares, and Black answers by capturing it in passing.

line.say: White's pawn jumps two squares and lands beside Black's pawn.
Black captures en passant: the pawn lands on e3 and the white pawn on e4 is removed.

claims.statement: The jump to e4 is legal.

steps.text: **Only right now.** The chance lasts for one move. Play something else and it is gone for good, even if the pawns do not change. It also needs a real jump: a pawn that steps only one square gives no en passant, even beside your pawn.

steps.caption: White ignores the chance and moves the king. A move later the chance is gone.

line.say: White plays a different move and does not capture.
Black replies. The pawn on d5 now stands beside White's pawn in an ordinary way: the chance has passed.

claims.statement: Capturing en passant is legal in this position, right now.

steps.caption: Black steps one square and lands beside White's pawn. A step is not a jump.

line.say: Black's pawn takes one step and lands beside White's pawn.
White's pawn can only walk ahead. There is no capture, because Black did not jump.

steps.text: **Your king still comes first.** En passant is a move like any other, so it may never leave your own king in check. Rarely, both pawns leave the same rank at once and open a line to your king. Then the capture is illegal, even with all three yeses. Check the king before you take.

**Model answer.** En passant is an optional pawn capture that exists only on the move right after an enemy pawn jumps two squares and lands right beside your pawn. You capture it as if it had stepped one square. If you wait, if it only stepped once, or if it was not beside your pawn, the chance is gone.

steps.prompt: Read the model answer, cover it, then explain en passant to a friend: the three questions and how long the chance lasts. Then answer one case: a pawn steps one square beside yours. Can you capture it?
